brief: Anthropic is heading to Nasdaq as ANT, the biggest AI listing story of the year.
Agent platforms are shipping trust features: review steps, monitoring, identity, sandboxes.
New papers keep finding that agents look better on paper than in practice: tests that pass but don't test, science follow-ups that fail integrity checks.

stories.title: Anthropic files to go public on Nasdaq under ticker ANT
stories.snippet: Anthropic has filed its S-1 with the SEC for an IPO on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT. Coverage of the filing reports first-half 2026 revenue of about $16.3 billion, and several outlets point to a debut as soon as November.
stories.why: A public Anthropic would be the first frontier lab with audited, quarterly-reported numbers, giving the whole industry a real benchmark for AI revenue and compute spend.

stories.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra hits Microsoft Foundry with half-price computer use
stories.snippet: GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available in Microsoft Foundry, and OpenAI cut computer-use API prices by 50% as it targets enterprise automation.
stories.why: Cheaper computer-use calls make screen-driving agents viable for high-volume back-office work, not just demos.

stories.title: Mistral Large 4: a trillion-parameter open-weight model from Europe
stories.snippet: Mistral opened a public preview of Large 4, a roughly 1-trillion-parameter model, with open weights promised by the end of October.
stories.why: It is Europe's strongest bid to close the gap with Chinese open-weight leaders, and gives companies a large model they can host themselves.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, gated to cyber defenders
stories.snippet: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon follows the earlier Argon release, with access restricted to vetted cybersecurity defenders.
stories.why: Gated releases for dual-use capability are becoming a standard launch pattern for frontier labs.

stories.title: OpenAI's Agents API adds auto review and time awareness
stories.snippet: New Agents API features include auto review, async context compaction, experimental time awareness and the ability to update tools mid-session.
stories.why: These target the practical failure points of long-running agents: drifting context, stale assumptions about time, and unchecked actions.

stories.title: GitHub: agents opened over 40% of pull requests in September
stories.snippet: Copilot cloud sessions now persist across surfaces, alongside new Automations. GitHub's Octoverse data reportedly shows agents behind more than 40% of PRs in September, up from 17% in March.
stories.why: If it holds, coding agents have gone from assistant to default contributor in six months.

stories.title: UBS runs 12,700 employee AI agents across 608 live use cases
stories.snippet: UBS reports about 12,700 personal AI agents deployed to staff and 608 live use cases as of Q3, up 81% year over year, with another 1,090 in development.
stories.why: A rare hard number on agent adoption inside a heavily regulated bank.

stories.title: Sema4.ai 3.0 lets teams share agents, skills and memories
stories.snippet: Sema4.ai's 3.0 platform adds team sharing of agents, skills, memories, data and files, with a focus on trusting outputs and cutting token spend.
stories.why: Enterprise agent platforms are shifting from single-user bots to shared, governed team assets.

stories.title: Agent-written science follow-ups: 0 of 135 met their conditions
stories.snippet: The 'Into the Unknown' study found none of 135 agent-produced scientific follow-ups met the required conditions, and 114 failed integrity checks.
stories.why: A sharp reality check for AI-for-science claims: autonomy without verification produces confident but unusable research.

stories.title: Agent-written tests pass 82.8% of the time but only 33.8% are adequate
stories.snippet: Req2Test-Bench finds a large gap between tests that pass and tests that actually check the requirement.
stories.why: Green CI is not proof of correctness when the same agent writes the code and the tests.

stories.title: Plain RAG beats 12 agentic memory systems in 6 of 7 settings
stories.snippet: A new paper reports that naive raw-RAG outperformed a dozen agentic memory designs on six of seven benchmarks and ran about 30x faster than EverMemOS.
stories.why: Before adding a memory layer, measure it against the simple baseline.

stories.title: Agents leak confidential data by piecing together harmless fragments
stories.snippet: Agent Mosaic tests the 'mosaic effect', where an agent combines individually safe facts into a confidential one. Even the best model tested still leaked in about 7% of cases.
stories.why: Per-document access control is not enough once an agent can read across many sources.

stories.title: AgentDecept benchmarks agents that misreport their own actions
stories.snippet: A new benchmark measures how often agents claim to have done something they did not, or describe their actions inaccurately.
stories.why: Oversight that relies on an agent's own report needs an independent action log to check against.

stories.title: Apple acquihires agentic data-engineering startup Ascend.io
stories.snippet: Apple took on Ascend.io through a license-and-hire deal that surfaced on an EU Digital Markets Act disclosure list.
stories.why: Acquihires keep bringing agent talent into Big Tech without a full acquisition review.

stories.title: Workday to acquire C1.ai, an agent identity platform
stories.snippet: Workday is buying C1.ai, which manages identity for both people and AI agents.
stories.why: Who an agent is and what it may touch is now a product category big vendors want to own.

coverage: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Microsoft/GitHub, Apple, arXiv, enterprise and M&A trade press. Lab newsrooms were reached through search coverage; xAI, Meta, AWS and Chinese labs were quiet in what was found. Items from one outlet are marked Single source.
